last_batch.research: PubMed E-utilities searches covered 30 final fresh non-prescription premenstrual-syndrome and dysmenorrhea topics. The main query set returned 161 unique PubMed PMIDs, 161 fetched article records, and 157 abstracts available for inspection. Retained numeric effects or valid relative effects were verified for PMIDs: 31780016, 41151539, 38613122, 36973702, 37447156, 35059756, 8623866, 39683510, 37165643, 26132140, 40671058, 34708460, 39887989, 39550537, 31383452, 29037637, 29529975, 37335817, 34996424, 24636695, 36686444, 30389956, 41790650, 35249825, and 39066557. Twenty-five retained references were new to the database. Fifteen new entries across fifteen qualified topics retain numeric intervention-versus-control results or valid relative effects. Ginger dysmenorrhea, cinnamon menstrual pain, fennel dysmenorrhea, magnesium premenstrual syndrome, and calcium premenstrual syndrome were linked to existing entries. Fenugreek, evening primrose premenstrual syndrome, black cohosh premenstrual syndrome, vitamin B1 premenstrual syndrome, vitamin E dysmenorrhea, ginger premenstrual syndrome, garlic dysmenorrhea, chamomile dysmenorrhea, peppermint dysmenorrhea, and tai chi premenstrual syndrome were screened out because the retrieved PubMed records did not provide a retained topic-specific numeric intervention-versus-control result or valid relative effect.
